Ask about Henrik Zetterberg's research

Answers are drawn only from Henrik Zetterberg's published papers listed on this page, with each point linked to its paper. They describe what the papers report, not personal views or advice from Henrik Zetterberg. This is not medical advice.

Try

Development and validation of fluid biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease and other forms of neurodegeneration.

  • Cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers. In patients with mild cognitive impairment, a CSF profile of low Aβ42 and elevated tau was strongly associated with incipient Alzheimer's disease over 4 to 6 years of follow-up.
  • Plasma phosphorylated tau. Co-developed and validated an ultrasensitive blood p-tau181 assay and evaluated plasma p-tau217, which distinguished Alzheimer's disease from other neurodegenerative disorders with high accuracy.
  • Neurofilament light. Showed that blood neurofilament light reflects neuroaxonal damage, including neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease and neuronal damage in multiple sclerosis.
  • Astrocytic markers. Found that plasma GFAP is an early marker of amyloid-β but not tau pathology, elevated already in cognitively unimpaired amyloid-positive individuals.

  1. 1
    AUC 0.96for blood p-tau217 in telling Alzheimer's from other dementias

    Plasma p-tau217 separated Alzheimer's dementia from other neurodegenerative diseases with an accuracy (AUC) of 0.96, better than p-tau181, NfL and MRI, and it identified Alzheimer's confirmed at autopsy with an AUC of 0.89.

    Palmqvist et al. 2020 · JAMACross-sectional study of 3 cohorts (autopsy cohort, BioFINDER-2 and a Colombian inherited Alzheimer's family), about 1,400 participants
  2. 2
    85% to 91%accuracy of a fully automated p-tau217 blood test in clinics

    A commercial, fully automated plasma p-tau217 test detected Alzheimer's pathology with 89% to 91% accuracy in memory clinics and 85% in primary care. Using two cutoffs raised accuracy to 92% to 94%, with 12% to 17% of people left in an uncertain middle range. Accuracy was lower in people aged 80 or older but was not affected by kidney disease, diabetes, sex or APOE genotype.

    Palmqvist et al. 2025 · Nat MedMulticohort diagnostic study, 1,767 people with cognitive symptoms in Sweden, Spain and Italy, including primary care
  3. 3
    AUC 0.92 to 0.97for a commercial p-tau217 blood test detecting amyloid and tau

    A commercially available plasma p-tau217 immunoassay identified abnormal amyloid (AUC 0.92 to 0.96) and tau (AUC 0.93 to 0.97) as well as spinal fluid tests did. A three-range cutoff cut the need for confirmatory testing by about 80%, and levels rose each year only in people with amyloid.

    Ashton et al. 2024 · JAMA NeurolCohort study across 3 cohorts (TRIAD, WRAP, SPIN), 786 participants
  4. 4
    ~90%of people with mild memory problems and abnormal spinal fluid developed Alzheimer's within 9 to 10 years

    In people with mild cognitive impairment followed for a median of 9.2 years, an abnormal spinal fluid Aβ42 to p-tau ratio predicted Alzheimer's dementia with 88% sensitivity and 90% specificity. Aβ42 was already fully lowered 5 to 10 years before dementia, while tau rose later.

    Buchhave et al. 2012 · Arch Gen PsychiatryClinical cohort, 137 patients with mild cognitive impairment, median 9.2 years of follow-up
  5. 5
    17.7×higher risk of Alzheimer's with abnormal spinal fluid tau and amyloid

    People with mild cognitive impairment whose spinal fluid showed high total tau and low Aβ42 had a 17.7-fold higher risk of developing Alzheimer's over 4 to 6 years. The combination detected those who went on to Alzheimer's with 95% sensitivity and 83% specificity, far more strongly than age, sex, education or APOE genotype.

    Hansson et al. 2006 · Lancet NeurolProspective cohort, 137 patients with mild cognitive impairment and 39 controls, about 5 years of follow-up
  6. 6
    AUC 0.83 → 0.91predicting Alzheimer's within 4 years from a blood test plus brief tests

    In people with memory complaints or mild cognitive impairment, plasma p-tau217 predicted Alzheimer's dementia within 4 years with an AUC of 0.83, rising to 0.91 when combined with brief memory and thinking tests and APOE genotype. Memory clinic doctors' own predictions reached an AUC of 0.71.

    Palmqvist et al. 2021 · Nat MedPrognostic study, 2 cohorts (BioFINDER 340 and ADNI 543 participants)
  7. 7
    8 yearsbefore death, blood p-tau181 already pointed to Alzheimer's at autopsy

    In people who all had an Alzheimer's diagnosis during life, plasma p-tau181 taken 8 years before death separated true Alzheimer's at autopsy from other brain diseases with an AUC of 97%. In Alzheimer's, the main rise in p-tau181 happened between 8 and 4 years before death.

    Lantero Rodriguez et al. 2020 · Acta NeuropatholLongitudinal autopsy cohort, 115 participants with blood samples 8, 4 and 2 years before death
  8. 8
    10,059 peopleshow spinal fluid NfL is raised in most brain diseases

    Pooling spinal fluid neurofilament light data from 10,059 people with 35 diagnoses, levels were higher than in healthy controls in most neurological conditions, highest in HIV with cognitive impairment, ALS, frontotemporal dementia and Huntington's disease. Levels rose with age and were often higher in men, so age- and sex-specific reference values may be needed.

    Bridel et al. 2019 · JAMA NeurolSystematic review and individual-level meta-analysis, 10,059 participants
  9. 9
    Togethermicroglial activation and tau spread through the brain

    Brain scans of 130 people across ageing and Alzheimer's showed that activated microglia, the brain's immune cells, and tau spread together in the same Braak-like stages. Tau spread over time followed the baseline microglia network, and having amyloid, tau and microglial activation together best predicted cognitive impairment.

    Pascoal et al. 2021 · Nat MedPET imaging study of microglia, amyloid and tau, 130 participants, with longitudinal follow-up
  10. 10
    231 studiesconfirm spinal fluid tau, p-tau and Aβ42 as core Alzheimer's markers

    Pooling 231 studies of 15,699 patients and 13,018 controls, spinal fluid total tau (2.5 times higher), p-tau (1.9 times) and Aβ42 (about half) strongly separated Alzheimer's from controls. Spinal fluid NfL and blood total tau also differed strongly, while many other proposed markers changed little.

    Olsson et al. 2016 · Lancet NeurolSystematic review and meta-analysis of 15 biomarkers, 231 studies
  11. 11
    AUC 0.78 → 0.91adding blood GFAP to detect amyloid in people with normal memory

    In cognitively normal older adults, plasma GFAP was much higher in those with amyloid on PET scans. A model of age, sex and APOE4 detected amyloid with an AUC of 0.78, which rose to 0.91 when plasma GFAP was added.

    Chatterjee et al. 2021 · Transl PsychiatryCross-sectional study, 96 cognitively normal older adults with amyloid PET
  12. 12
    AUC 0.76for blood GFAP flagging amyloid build-up

    Plasma GFAP, a marker of reactive astrocytes, was raised in every amyloid-positive group, including people with normal memory, and was linked to amyloid but not tau after accounting for each other. It predicted a positive amyloid scan with an AUC of 0.76, better than GFAP in spinal fluid.

    Pereira et al. 2021 · BrainCross-sectional and longitudinal analysis in BioFINDER-2, 504 participants
  13. 13
    AUC 0.947for the best of 10 blood p-tau tests

    Comparing 10 plasma p-tau tests in people with mild cognitive impairment, a mass spectrometry p-tau217 test was best at detecting amyloid (AUC 0.947) and predicting progression to Alzheimer's dementia (AUC 0.932). Among antibody-based tests, a p-tau217 assay scored highest (AUC about 0.89).

    Janelidze et al. 2023 · BrainHead-to-head comparison, 135 patients with mild cognitive impairment, 4.9 years of follow-up
  14. 14
    8 assayscompared for blood amyloid; mass spectrometry did best

    Of 8 plasma Aβ42/40 tests, certain mass spectrometry methods detected abnormal brain amyloid best (AUC about 0.86), while most antibody-based tests reached 0.64 to 0.78. Results were replicated in a second cohort.

    Janelidze et al. 2021 · JAMA NeurolHead-to-head comparison in BioFINDER and ADNI, 408 participants
  15. 15
    p-tau217 firstamong leading commercial Alzheimer's blood tests

    Comparing commercial blood tests from six companies on the same samples, p-tau217 measures most accurately classified amyloid and tau status, while plasma Aβ42/40 had relatively low accuracy for amyloid. P-tau217 also tracked cortical thinning better than NfL.

    Schindler et al. 2024 · Alzheimers DementHead-to-head comparison of commercial assays in ADNI plasma samples
  16. 16
    Ratio beats Aβ42spinal fluid Aβ42/40 is a better Alzheimer's marker

    Across 3 cohorts and 3 different assays, spinal fluid Aβ42/40 and Aβ42/38 ratios predicted an abnormal amyloid scan better than Aβ42 alone and better separated Alzheimer's from Lewy body, Parkinson's and vascular dementia.

    Janelidze et al. 2016 · Ann Clin Transl NeurolDiagnostic study in 3 cohorts, 1,182 participants
  17. 17
    750 patientsmulticentre test of spinal fluid markers in mild memory problems

    Across 12 centres in Europe and the US, spinal fluid Aβ42, total tau and p-tau predicted which people with mild cognitive impairment developed Alzheimer's with AUCs of 0.76 to 0.79. The Aβ42 test varied considerably between centres, showing the need for standardisation.

    Mattsson et al. 2009 · JAMAMulticentre prospective cohort, 750 patients with mild cognitive impairment, 529 with Alzheimer's and 304 controls
  18. 18
    10 + 4 + 6 yearspreclinical, prodromal and dementia stages at age 70

    For a 70-year-old with preclinical Alzheimer's, the estimated duration was 10 years before symptoms, 4 years of mild symptoms and 6 years of dementia. Total disease length ranged from 24 years when it starts at 60 to 15 years at 80, and was shorter in men, APOE4 carriers and people with abnormal spinal fluid tau.

    Vermunt et al. 2019 · Alzheimers DementMultistate modelling across 6 cohorts, 3,268 participants
  19. 19
    p-tau rises earlywhen amyloid changes are still subtle

    New spinal fluid p-tau181, p-tau217 and p-tau231 tests rose more clearly than a standard p-tau test in the preclinical stage, when only subtle amyloid changes were present, and separated amyloid-positive from amyloid-negative people with normal memory.

    Suárez-Calvet et al. 2020 · EMBO Mol MedCross-sectional biomarker study in a preclinical Alzheimer's cohort
  20. 20
    Higher NfLin spinal fluid predicts faster atrophy and decline

    Spinal fluid neurofilament light was higher in Alzheimer's dementia and mild cognitive impairment than in healthy controls. In mild cognitive impairment, higher levels went with faster whole-brain and hippocampal shrinkage and faster decline on memory tests.

    Zetterberg et al. 2016 · JAMA NeurolCohort study in ADNI, 397 participants
  21. 21
    AUC 0.91for blood NfL separating Parkinson's from atypical parkinsonism

    Blood neurofilament light was higher in multiple system atrophy, progressive supranuclear palsy and corticobasal syndrome than in Parkinson's disease, and separated Parkinson's from these atypical disorders with AUCs of 0.81 to 0.91 across 3 cohorts, including early disease.

    Hansson et al. 2017 · NeurologyDiagnostic study, 3 prospective cohorts, 504 participants
  22. 22
    NfL in MSblood NfL tracks lesions, relapses and disability

    In multiple sclerosis, serum neurofilament light was higher than in healthy controls, rose with active brain and spinal cord lesions, fell under disease-modifying treatment, and levels above the 97.5th percentile of controls predicted more relapses and worsening disability.

    Disanto et al. 2017 · Ann NeurolTwo MS cohorts (142 cross-sectional, 246 longitudinal) and 254 controls
  23. 23
    NfL in Huntington'sblood NfL rises stage by stage and predicts decline

    Carriers of the Huntington's disease mutation had higher plasma neurofilament light than controls, the gap grew with each disease stage, and baseline levels predicted later decline in thinking, daily function and brain volume.

    Byrne et al. 2017 · Lancet NeurolRetrospective analysis of the TRACK-HD study, 201 mutation carriers and 97 controls
  24. 24
    Tau doublesin blood after concussion in ice hockey players

    Professional ice hockey players with concussion had blood total tau of 10.0 pg/mL compared with 4.5 pg/mL before the season, along with raised S100B. Levels peaked right after the injury and fell during rehabilitation.

    Shahim et al. 2014 · JAMA NeurolMulticentre prospective cohort, Swedish Hockey League, 288 players (35 concussions)
  25. 25
    GFAP then NfLbrain injury markers rise in severe COVID-19

    Patients with severe COVID-19 had higher blood GFAP and NfL than controls. GFAP peaked early and then fell, while NfL kept rising, suggesting an early astrocyte response followed by later nerve fibre injury.

    Kanberg et al. 2020 · NeurologyCohort study, 47 patients with COVID-19 and 33 controls
  26. 26
    27%of thinking decline explained by a synapse protein ratio beyond amyloid and tau

    Spinal fluid proteomics in 3,397 people found that a synapse protein ratio, YWHAG:NPTX2, explained 27% of the variation in cognitive impairment beyond amyloid and tau. It rose about 20 years before expected symptoms in inherited Alzheimer's and predicted progression from normal cognition to mild cognitive impairment (hazard ratio 3.0 per standard deviation).

    Oh et al. 2025 · Nat MedCSF proteomics across 6 cohorts, 3,397 participants, up to 15 years of follow-up
  27. 27
    No benefitof oral semaglutide in early Alzheimer's

    In two phase 3 trials of 3,808 people with early Alzheimer's, oral semaglutide did not slow decline on the CDR-SB scale over 104 weeks compared with placebo.

    Cummings et al. 2026 · LancetTwo randomised placebo-controlled phase 3 trials (evoke and evoke+), 3,808 participants

About this page

This page gathers Henrik Zetterberg's published papers and preprints from PubMed and Europe PMC. The summary and key findings are written from those papers, and every finding cites exactly one of them.

"Most important" puts the findings with the widest relevance first. "Newest" sorts by the year of each finding's paper.

This site is for education and is not medical advice.
